newsitem.title: USA: USDA - 96/97 world cocoa bean output 2.66 mln MT.
newsitem.headline: USDA - 96/97 world cocoa bean output 2.66 mln MT.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department Tuesday forecast world cocoa bean production for the 1996/97 season at 2.66 million tonnes, down eight percent from last year's revised record outturn of 2.88 million tonnes.
USDA said the reduction is based on projections of smaller harvests in the Ivory Coast, Ghana, Brazil, Malaysia and Cameroon.
In its World Agricultural Production report, USDA pegged the Ivory Coast 1996/97 cocoa crop at 1.05 million tonnes, down 12 percent from a record 1.20 million tonnes in 1995/96.

It said the decrease seen for the Ivory Coast, the world's largest cocoa bean producer, was due in part to heavy rains from May through August that destroyed blossoms and young pods, especially in the southern and eastern growing areas.
USDA said the 1996/97 Ivory Coast forecast consists of 900,000 tonnes of main crop production, including 50,000 tonnes held over from the 1995/96 mid crop, and 150,000 tonnes of mid-crop beans.
It estimated Ghana 1996/97 cocoa bean production at 390,000 tonnes, a decrease of seven percent from last season's revised estimate of 420,000 tonnes.

USDA said this was a normal cyclical decline following the large volume of beans harvested during the 1995/96 season. It said Ghana's main crop harvest, which begins in late October, is forecast at 350,000 tonnes and pegged the 1996/97 mid-crop, to be harvested from May-June 1997, at 40,000 tonnes.
USDA pegged the Brazil crop at 198,000 tonnes, down 12 percent from the revised 1995/96 estimate of 225,000 tonnes.

"Inclement weather, the continued spread of the witches- broom fungus, and strained farmer finances are the key reasons why Brazil's 1996/97 cocoa bean crop may end up being the smallest one recorded since the 1972/73 harvest of 158,000 tonnes," USDA said in the report.

It estimated 1996/97 Indonesia cocoa bean output at 280,000 tonnes, up from 275,000 tonnes for 1995/96, pegged Nigeria outturn at 150,000 tonnes, up from 140,000 tonnes for 1995/96 and forecast Malaysia output at 120,000 tonnes versus 125,000 seen for 1995/96.
